reasoning: Set A sticks closely to the ground truth. Its fish tank is circular and fish are scored on survival. It has one learning predator with self-play against an opponent pool and a cross-play table. Its ladders run tabular → DQN → CNN and REINFORCE → PPO, with ablations and a library reference for each stage. Its test oracles are very rigorous: TC-07, TC-12, TC-42, TC-52 and TC-58 all check out by hand, and truncation vs termination is handled correctly in GAE. A has three main weaknesses. First, each stage is one very large milestone rather than a walking skeleton. Second, the M1 interface task freezes stage-2 and stage-3 symbols (FishTank, PPOAgent, OpponentPool, the predator-prey fields in RunSettings) that no M1 task builds, which clashes with the CR-02 no-stub exit check. Third, some text is stale: the brief's 'Not doing: designing future environments now' and the CONSTRAINTS boundaries, which leave out selfplay. Set B scopes its interface better: only M1 symbols are frozen, and unfrozen ones are listed explicitly. Its spines are real baselines (online Q-learning, REINFORCE as the PPO spine), its check-world gate is a good idea, and S2 is split cleanly into one fish → many fish → local sight. But B departs from the user's project: the tank is square, fish are scored on hits with respawn instead of survival, predator-prey has 2 predators, and there is no self-play against past opponents. Its milestone IDs run out of order (M4 is built after M6). M2 is a leftover bundle of replay, reference check, write-ups and the full DQN, so M1 does not let the user watch a replay. Some of B's packets also have gaps: the Snake task's packet leaves out WorldSpec, TeamSpec and ActionSpace, and the PL-02 wiring smoke command `rllab train` actually runs through the PL-03 batch, which isn't wired yet. On balance, A's RL soundness, completeness and buildable packets outweigh B's better milestone and interface scoping.

strengths: Faithful to the user's three environments: circular tank, survival scoring, one learning predator, and self-play with an opponent pool plus cross-play
Each stage has a clear RL ladder (tabular/DQN/CNN; REINFORCE/PPO; fixed → naive co-learning → pool), with ablations and a library reference
Golden cases are precise and hand-checkable, with cited sources (Sutton & Barto, GAE, PPO)
Context packets include every needed type, test case and sample reference, e.g. M1-T13 and M1-T21
Ideas docs record why stages 2 and 3 look the way they do
weaknesses: M1 covers the whole Snake stage (31 tasks) instead of starting with a walking skeleton
The M1 interface freezes M2/M3 types and step stubs that no M1 task owns
Stale framing in the brief and in the CONSTRAINTS boundaries
The contract is very long (about 460 lines) and RunSettings is overloaded with fields for later stages

strengths: Interface freezes only M1 symbols, and the unfrozen boundaries are listed explicitly
Spines are real minimal baselines (online Q-learning; REINFORCE as the PPO spine)
Check-world gate (two-exit corridor) catches silent RL bugs before any batch
S2 is split cleanly along dependency lines (one fish → many → local sight)
Paired permutation test with Holm correction is fully specified
weaknesses: Departs from ground truth: square tank, hit/respawn scoring instead of survival, 2 predators, no self-play against past opponents
Milestone IDs run out of build order (M4 comes after M6), and M2 is a leftover bundle
M1 has no replay, even though watching a replay is a core success criterion
Some packets leave out needed types, and one wiring smoke command depends on an unwired pipeline
No exploration or reward ablations, so fewer of the concepts the user named are actually taught
